idiom_name: WorkManager OneTimeWorkRequest with network constraint and BackoffPolicy (Android)
implementation_notes: On Android the durable local store is WorkManager's internally managed SQLite database: an enqueued WorkRequest survives app restarts and device reboots and is rescheduled by the system, so the platform plays both the store and the forwarder, and BackoffPolicy.EXPONENTIAL (with WorkRequest.DEFAULT_BACKOFF_DELAY_MILLIS and the min/max bounds) is the retry policy. A Worker returns Result.retry() while the peer is unreachable and Result.success() after the acknowledgement, and constraints such as NetworkType.CONNECTED express 'forward when the link is back'. On the JVM the same role belongs to a JMS/broker client or an outbox table; the classic hand-written spool is justified only when the work must not be deferred to WorkManager's scheduling (or the app is not Android), and coroutines/Channel are never the store because they die with the process.
code_sketch:
val request = OneTimeWorkRequestBuilder<ForwardWorker>()
    .setConstraints(Constraints.Builder()
        .setRequiredNetworkType(NetworkType.CONNECTED).build())
    .setBackoffCriteria(BackoffPolicy.EXPONENTIAL, 30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .setInputData(workDataOf("id" to id, "payload" to payload))
    .build()
WorkManager.getInstance(context).enqueue(request)   // durable across reboots
// ForwardWorker.doWork(): deliver() -> Result.success() else Result.retry()
pitfalls: WorkManager is for deferrable, guaranteed work: an in-process coroutine or Channel queue is not durable and must never be used as the spool.
Returning Result.failure() (or throwing) drops the work; only Result.retry() triggers the backoff schedule.
ExistingWorkPolicy and unique work names change retry semantics - REPLACE discards a pending retry together with its backoff state.
A Worker runs under a time budget (about ten minutes, less for expedited work); long uploads must be chunked or made resumable.
